articles.title: Chasing a -O2 pessimization in antcc
articles.summary: Chasing a -O2 pessimization in antcc, a compiler for Lua, has revealed a surprising issue where the generated code is 1.4x slower than the optimized version, despite the compiler not implementing many optimizations. The problem lies in the function luaV_execute, which is the main bytecode interpreter loop for the Lua VM, and is a huge function with a hot loop, many cases/control flow branches, and nested graph structures that can pessimize the whole loop. The inlining thresholds have been tweaked, but the issue persists, and the final codegen is only 11% bigger than the -O1 IR, suggesting that instruction selection and register allocation are the main culprits.

articles.title: Who is vfmaddrnd231pd??
articles.summary: vfmaddrnd231pd is a unique instruction from the FMA instruction set that allows for controlled rounding of floating-point values, enabling faster algorithms that rely on rounding. Most x86 floating-point instructions use the global rounding mode, which can be slow, but vfmaddrnd231pd enables per-instruction control, allowing for faster algorithms. However, the Intel Software Development Manual documents it as VFMADDRND231PD, and the instruction is absent in the 2026 edition of the manual, despite being present in the 2024 edition. This raises questions about the origin and intended purpose of the instruction.
